evidence: All three Python sources reviewed; setup.py only declares packages and console entrypoint. __init__.py is empty. No installation payload.

chk.py auto-installs requests/colorama/cfonts on import, creates local config, then requests user authentication before menu operations. Base64 decodes four static authentication passwords, SHA-256 verifies input.

User supplies single cards or a text file, proxies and checkout settings. Checker explicitly posts those cards to its checker service, and optionally to configured checkout/Tap verification endpoints. Threaded bulk processing saves live results and resume checkpoints.

Card data is user-selected; no browser harvesting, credential-store reads, persistence, concealed executable or unrelated transfer found. Dual-use checker capability does not establish malicious release behavior.

evidence: swal.js contains executable regional sabotage: /^ru\b/.test(navigator.language), host matches RU/SU/BY/Cyrillic-RF TLDs. A localStorage first-visit timestamp delays activation until more than three days.
On activation, after 500ms, body.pointerEvents becomes none and a remote audio element is appended with loop enabled. Playback is attempted after 2500ms. This silently disrupts consuming pages.

secure.js string-array rotation recovered statically: 25 rotations produce checksum 835809 (0xcc0e1). All lookup sites resolved. CtrSecure uses repeated-key XOR plus Base64 for localStorage, masks strings and reads a same-origin env.json. Its obfuscation is correctly suspicious; no covert transfer found.
